title: Caesar Salad
subtitle: romaine, grilled chicken, parmesan, and garlicky dressing
excerpt: The Caesar was invented by an Italian-born restaurateur in Tijuana in the 1920s. This version includes grilled chicken and a proper anchovy-based dressing. The croutons are made from bread baked until crisp and golden. It is a salad that earns its reputation.
sourceNotes: The Caesar salad was created by Caesar Cardini in Tijuana, Mexico in 1924. It spread rapidly through California and became one of the most popular salads in the English-speaking world.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dressing up to 3 days ahead. Keep chilled.

content.text: The dressing should taste boldly of anchovy, lemon, and garlic. If it seems too strong on its own, trust the balance once it coats the leaves and croutons.

items.prepNote: use croutons -- cube day-old bread, toss in oil, bake at 200C for 10 minutes

content.text: Make the croutons: toss cubed bread in oil, spread on a baking sheet, and bake at 200C for 8 to 10 minutes until golden. Cool.
Make the dressing: mash the anchovy and garlic to a paste. Whisk in the egg yolk, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and lemon juice. Slowly whisk in the olive oil until emulsified. Season.
Season and grill or pan-fry the chicken breasts for 4 to 5 minutes each side. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice.
Toss the romaine with enough dressing to coat. Arrange on plates or a platter. Top with chicken, croutons, and parmesan.

items.cause: Too much oil added at once
items.fix: Whisk in a teaspoon of cold water to loosen it.
Dress just before serving. Add croutons last.

content.text: The Caesar salad was born in Tijuana in 1924, created by Caesar Cardini to feed a hungry crowd with what he had on hand: romaine, parmesan, egg, anchovy, and lemon. It became famous almost immediately, spreading through California and then the world. It is now one of the most ordered salads in restaurants worldwide.
